title: D. Inversion Value of a Permutation
statement:
A permutation of length $$n$$ is an array of $$n$$ integers, where each number from $$1$$ to $$n$$ appears exactly once. An inversion in a permutation $$p$$ is a pair of indices $$(i, j)$$ such that $$i  \lt  j$$ and $$p_i  \gt  p_j$$.

For a permutation $$p$$, we define its inversion value as the number of its subsegments that contain at least one inversion. Formally, this is the number of pairs of integers $$(l, r)$$ ($$1 $\leq l  \lt  r \leq n$$$) for which there exists a pair of indices $$(i, j)$$ satisfying the following conditions: $$l $\leq i  \lt  j \leq r$$$ and $$p_i  \gt  p_j$$.

For example, for the permutation $$[3, 1, 4, 2]$$, the inversion value is $$5$$.

You are given two integers $$n$$ and $$k$$. Your task is to construct a permutation of length $$n$$ with an inversion value equal to exactly $$k$$ .

The first line contains one integer $$t$$ ($$1 $\leq t \leq 500$$$) — the number of test cases.

Each test case consists of a single line containing two integers $$n$$ and $$k$$ ($$2 $\leq n \leq 30$$$; $$0 $\leq k \leq \dfrac{n(n-1)}{2}$$$).

For each test case, output the answer as follows:
input: Input The first line contains one integer $$t$$ ($$1 $\leq t \leq 500$$$) — the number of test cases. Each test case consists of a single line containing two integers $$n$$ and $$k$$ ($$2 $\leq n \leq 30$$$; $$0 $\leq k \leq \dfrac{n(n-1)}{2}$$$).
output: Output For each test case, output the answer as follows: if the desired permutation does not exist, output a single integer $$0$$; otherwise, output $$n$$ distinct integers from $$1$$ to $$n$$ — the desired permutation. If there are multiple such permutations, you may output any of them.
